title: Body wall and gut wall layers

objective.text: Distinguish the somatopleure from the splanchnopleure.

body.general: Once the cavity opens, the middle layer (mesoderm) around it is in two sheets [f1,f3]. The outer sheet, the parietal layer, lies against the outer layer (ectoderm) and runs over the amnion [f1]. With the ectoderm it is the somatopleure, which builds the body wall [f2]. The inner sheet, the visceral (splanchnic) layer, lies against the inner layer (endoderm) and runs over the yolk sac [f3]. With the endoderm it is the splanchnopleure, which builds the gut wall [f4]. In folding, the inner sheet rolls in with the gut; the somatopleure forms the side walls [f5].
body.mbbs: The parietal (somatic) layer of lateral plate mesoderm lies next to the surface ectoderm [f1]. It is continuous with the extraembryonic mesoderm covering the amnion [f1]. Parietal mesoderm plus ectoderm form the somatopleure, which builds the body wall [f2]. The visceral (splanchnic) layer lies next to the endoderm [f3]. It is continuous with the extraembryonic mesoderm covering the yolk sac [f3]. Visceral mesoderm plus endoderm form the splanchnopleure, which builds the gut wall [f4]. During folding the visceral layer rolls ventrally with the gut tube [f5]. The parietal layer and ectoderm form the lateral body-wall folds [f5].

facts.text: The parietal (somatic) layer of lateral plate mesoderm lies next to the surface ectoderm and is continuous with the extraembryonic mesoderm over the amnion.
Parietal mesoderm together with the ectoderm is the somatopleure, which builds the body wall.
The visceral (splanchnic) layer lies next to the endoderm and is continuous with the extraembryonic mesoderm over the yolk sac.
Visceral mesoderm together with the endoderm is the splanchnopleure, which builds the gut wall.
During folding the visceral layer rolls ventrally with the gut tube, while the parietal layer and ectoderm form the lateral body-wall folds.

misconceptions.wrong: The somatopleure is the same as the somites (blocks beside the future spinal cord).
misconceptions.right: The somatopleure is the parietal layer plus ectoderm (the body wall); somites are separate blocks beside the future spinal cord.
The splanchnopleure (the visceral layer plus endoderm) builds the gut wall; the somatopleure builds the body wall.

checks.prompt: Which forms the lateral body-wall folds during folding?
checks.why: As the embryo folds, the somatopleure forms the side walls of the body.

checks.prompt: Which pair makes up the somatopleure?
checks.why: Somato- = body: the parietal layer and the ectoderm it touches. Somites are separate blocks.

checks.prompt: A mesoderm layer lies against the endoderm and runs on over the yolk sac. With the endoderm, what does it build?
checks.why: That is the visceral layer; with the endoderm it is the splanchnopleure, the gut wall.

adult: The somatopleure becomes the body wall and the splanchnopleure becomes the wall of the gut [f2,f4].

remember.q: What is the somatopleure, and what does it build?
remember.a: The parietal layer plus ectoderm; it builds the body wall [f2].

remember.q: What is the splanchnopleure, and what does it build?
remember.a: The visceral layer plus endoderm; it builds the gut wall [f4].

remember.q: Over which sac does each layer run on?
remember.a: Parietal layer over the amnion (the fluid sac round the embryo); visceral layer over the yolk sac [f1,f3].
